label: long-state-truncated
state: The quarterly report covers revenue, churn, support volume and infrastructure cost across every region. Revenue grew in the north and west, held flat in the south, and declined in the east after the loss of two enterprise accounts. Churn rose slightly among small customers who cited price, while enterprise churn fell. Support volume doubled during the outage in the second month, when the primary database failed over twice and the status page lagged the incident by forty minutes. Infrastructure cost rose eleven percent, mostly from the new replication cluster that the outage review recommended. The review also asked for a rewritten on-call runbook, a staged rollout policy for schema changes, and a monthly failover drill. Customer sentiment in surveys recovered by the end of the quarter, but the enterprise pipeline is thinner than planned and the sales team has asked for two additional solution engineers. Finance recommends holding hiring flat outside of sales and reliability until the pipeline recovers. Legal flagged one contract with an auto-renewal clause that conflicts with the new pricing policy and asked for a decision before the renewal date next month. The board meeting is scheduled for the first week of next quarter and the deck is due ten days before it. The report ends with an appendix of regional metrics, a list of open incidents, and a note that the east region manager has resigned effective at the end of the month, which leaves the region without a lead during the renewal season. The quarterly report covers revenue, churn, support volume and infrastructure cost across every region, repeated here so that the state runs past the model's maximum length and is truncated from the right. Appendix A lists regional metrics. The north closed the quarter at one hundred and twelve percent of target, driven by three mid-market renewals and a new logistics customer. The west closed at one hundred and four percent, with most growth from expansion inside existing accounts rather than new logos. The south was flat: new bookings matched churn almost exactly, and the regional team attributes the stall to a competitor that cut prices by a fifth in the spring. The east closed at eighty one percent after the two enterprise losses, and its pipeline for next quarter covers only sixty percent of target. Appendix B lists open incidents. Incident 4471 concerns intermittent latency in the reporting service under month-end load and remains under investigation. Incident 4480 concerns a billing export that dropped rows with non-ASCII customer names; a fix is written but not yet deployed. Incident 4492 concerns an expired certificate on a legacy integration endpoint that two customers still use; the owners have been notified. Appendix C records decisions taken during the quarter, including the move to annual pricing reviews, the retirement of the legacy mobile client, and the freeze on discretionary travel, which finance proposes to lift once the enterprise pipeline recovers to at least eighty percent of plan.
